transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Evan Moore (Redwood AE), Sofia Lin (Redwood SE), James Carter (Quasar CTO), Leila Ahmed (Quasar ML Eng), Marco Ruiz (Quasar DevOps)

Auto-generated Summary: quickstart + credits + security questions; medium transcription quality.

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Evan from Redwood, this is Sofia our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
[00:06] James: Good, thanks. Quick morning for us, appreciate you squeezing this in.
[00:10] Leila: Hi all. We're excited to see what Redwood's quickstart looks like.
[00:15] Sofia: Awesome. We're going to cover the self-serve Hosted API quickstart, what free credits get you, and then high-level differences to Dedicated and Private deployments \u2014 and leave time for your security/infra questions.
[00:25] Marco: Should be great. Our main ask is time-to-first-token and how much work to get an initial chat prototype in prod-ish conditions.

[00:35] Evan: Perfect. To set context, you told us you want a customer-facing chat assistant for your web app, must be GDPR-friendly, sub-200ms tail latency for search queries, and a phased rollout \u2014 is that still right?
[00:42] James: Yeah, that's right. Latency is a big one; also cost per 1M tokens is important \u2014 we're balancing user experience versus operating cost.

[00:50] Sofia: Great \u2014 so with Redwood Hosted API (our PLG self-serve) you can sign up, claim free credits, and get tokens in minutes. Time-to-first-token for a basic curl quickstart is typically under 10 minutes if you have your API key. The quickstart repo has SDK snippets for Node/Python, plus streaming examples.
[01:15] Leila: When you say streaming, is that server-sent-events or websockets? Any sample?
[01:20] Sofia: We support chunked streaming over HTTP/2 and SSE examples in the quickstart. I'll send the link after: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart (link shared).
[01:30] Evan: Also note the free credits tier \u2014 it's usually enough for experimenting and a small POC. We give a credits bundle tied to signup; if you want a trial for a larger trial we can extend.
[01:40] James: Do you require a card? For procurement, we prefer invoices for enterprise trials.
[01:45] Evan: For self-serve hosted signups we do ask for a card, but we can issue invoice credits for enterprise pilots \u2014 that's part of the next-step paperwork.

[02:00] Marco: How much engineering time to integrate? We have an existing infra with k8s, and we also want to host some data in our VPC.
[02:08] Sofia: For a basic integration using the Hosted API, it's just an HTTP call or SDK call. We have sample serverless templates too. If you need VPC peering or a Private deployment, that adds infra work \u2014 Private is typically a multi-week engagement for on-prem or VPC control plane. Dedicated is a middle ground \u2014 reserved GPU pools with predictable capacity and private networking options.
[02:35] Leila: For model selection: do you manage the models? We're worried about reproducibility and model rollouts.
[02:40] Sofia: Yes \u2014 Hosted gives you a model catalog with pinned versions. You can pin model versions in the API request so rollouts are predictable. For Dedicated and Private you get more control to pin quantized variants and we support canary rollouts.
[02:55] James: Any built-in caching? We expect a lot of prefix reuse.
[03:00] Sofia: We have prefix/KV caching in the runtime to reduce token compute. That helps cost without harming tail latency for many workloads.

[03:20] Evan: Let's talk numbers real quick \u2014 rough latency: Hosted low-contention tail can be 80-180ms token latency for smaller models, depends on seq length. Dedicated can be tuned for better throughput and more consistent tail latency depending on the GPU and batch config.
[03:40] Marco: And cost? We're trying to compare Hosted per-token against Dedicated reserved capacity.
[03:46] Evan: Hosted is usage billed; Dedicated is a commit with lower per-token unit economics at higher volume. I can send a simple T-shirt sizing spreadsheet that shows break-even points. Sofia will attach that.
[03:58] Sofia: Yep, will share the Dedicated sizing sheet. For PLG quickstarts most teams experiment on Hosted then move to Dedicated once traffic and SLA needs justify it.

[04:12] Leila: Security: we need SOC2 Type II, audit logs, SSO integration (SAML), and encryption with customer KMS. Does Redwood support those?
[04:20] Sofia: We are SOC2 and we support SAML SSO for the Console, RBAC, and audit logs. For encryption, Hosted uses server-side encryption; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. For data residency, Private or Dedicated in-region is the way to go.
[04:40] James: Do you retain prompts/outputs by default? Our legal team is picky about storage.
[04:44] Evan: By default we retain logs for X days for debugging; you can configure retention, and Private deployments let you keep data entirely on-prem. I'll include our security whitepaper and retention policy.

[05:00] Marco: From infra perspective, if we go Hosted but want VPC peering for embeddings to talk to our DB, is that supported?
[05:08] Sofia: Hosted doesn't do VPC peering to customer networks, but Dedicated offers private networking and VPC options. Private gives full customer-managed networking.

[05:20] Leila: What's the ramp for SEA and EMEA? We have users in EU and APAC.
[05:25] Evan: We have hosted regions in NA and EU; APAC is available via partners/Private deployments. We can discuss region-specific SLAs if that's a hard requirement.

[05:40] James: Ok good. Regarding evaluation \u2014 we'd like to do a quick POC focused on latency and cost per session. How would you recommend we start?
[05:48] Sofia: Start with PLG quickstart on Hosted: sign up, claim credits, run the quicktest harness we provide. It includes end-to-end tokenized prompts, sample payloads, and a perf harness. Time-to-first-token is minutes; time-to-basic-eval with a small cohort should be <48 hours.
[06:08] Leila: For the perf harness, does it do batching and KV cache simulation?
[06:12] Sofia: Yes the harness can replay request traces, simulate different batch sizes, and measure tail latency. We'll share the harness repo link.

[06:25] Evan: Also important \u2014 function calling and structured outputs. If you need deterministic JSON outputs or tool calls, the API supports schema guidance and function/tool calling. That helps reduce hallucination in assistant flows.
[06:40] Leila: Great. One of our concerns is model drift and evals \u2014 can Redwood hook into our eval pipelines to alert on regressions?
[06:46] Sofia: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. For Hosted PLG, you can integrate evals and set up alerts; for Dedicated/Private we can map that into your observability stack.

[07:05] Marco: A question about rate limiting and quotas \u2014 we need hard limits per-route to protect downstream.
[07:10] Evan: We support per-route quotas, rate limits, and token-level breakdowns in the Console. You can also set soft and hard limits per API key.

[07:20] James: Do you have customers in our vertical? We are in fintech, fairly regulated.
[07:25] Evan: We have several fintech customers on Dedicated and Private deployments; we'll anonymize references and share a short case study if that's helpful.

[07:35] Sofia: Back to quickstart \u2014 the signup flow gives you an API key. Example curl: curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-1.0\", \"input\":\"Hello\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \u2014 that will stream back tokens if you enable streaming.
[07:58] Leila: Any gotchas on CORS in browser demos?
[08:02] Sofia: We generally recommend a server-side token exchange to avoid exposing keys in the browser. Quickstart repo includes examples for serverless tokens.

[08:18] James: Timeline-wise, we are targeting an internal alpha in mid-May and public beta by end of Q3.
[08:25] Evan: That timeline fits our pattern: Hosted quickstart and POC in April, Dedicated sizing and procurement in late April/May if you move forward.

[08:36] Marco: What about compliance docs \u2014 SOC2, penetration test results, data processing addendum?
[08:42] Evan: We'll share SOC2 report redacted, PEN test summary, and a standard DPA. I'll attach in the follow-up.

[09:00] Leila: For measuring cost, we want a sample session cost calc. Do you provide a calculator?
[09:06] Sofia: We have a simple per-session cost spreadsheet: tokens/session times per-token price plus bandwidth. We'll include typical numbers for small, medium, large models. The Dedicated sheet shows commit vs usage math.

[09:24] James: Let's talk about Dedicated briefly \u2014 if we run a Dedicated pool, how does model updates work? We can't have rollouts surprise us.
[09:31] Sofia: You pin model versions in the route config. We support canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallback. For Dedicated you control the upgrade window and testing before traffic shift.

[09:48] Marco: Any limitations on model types or quantization?
[09:52] Sofia: We support a catalog of curated open models and optimizations for quantized variants. Some bleeding-edge model forks may need extra onboarding work.

[10:05] Evan: I want to capture the customer's success criteria: 1) <200ms tail latency for search-originated queries, 2) cost below $X per 1M tokens (James to confirm X), 3) SOC2 and KMS support, 4) regional hosting for EU.
[10:22] James: Yep that's accurate. I need to confirm the exact $ target.

[10:30] Leila: For the POC we'd like to test two flows: a short Q&A flow and a longer context summarization. Preferably run both on Hosted to get baseline.
[10:38] Sofia: Makes sense. We'll provide the harness with both flow templates.

[10:45] Evan: Ok let's do a quick live demo of signing up and the Console so you can see where keys and metrics live \u2014 run through a quick generate call and the streaming output.
[10:55] [demo noise \u2014 screen share described]
[11:10] Sofia: (typing) I'm pasting the quickstart link in the chat: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart and the Dedicated sizing sheet: https://redwood.sheets/sizing-example (placeholder).
[11:22] James: I like that the Console shows token breakdown; that will help cost ops.
[11:28] Marco: Can we get an example of the audit log format?
[11:31] Evan: Yes \u2014 I'll share a sample audit log extract in the follow-up.
[11:38] Leila: Also, can we try a short perf run with our sample prompts? What's needed from us?
[11:43] Sofia: Send us a small trace of representative requests (anonymized). We can replay it through the harness to estimate tail latency and cost.
[11:50] James: We'll prepare that; Marco will own.
[11:54] Marco: Yep will do.
[11:57] Evan: Great. Any other blockers?
[12:00] Leila: Procurement will want an invoice-based pilot if we move beyond free credits.
[12:04] Evan: We can accommodate that; I'll coordinate with our sales ops.
[12:09] James: One last question: does Redwood offer on-prem deployment entirely air-gapped?
[12:13] Sofia: Yes, the Private deployment option supports on-prem / air-gapped installs for regulated customers, though that involves an enterprise engagement and longer lead time.
[12:24] Evan: Awesome. Recap of next steps: Evan to send quickstart + free credits instructions and SOC2/DPA; Sofia to send Dedicated sizing sheet and perf harness link; Quasar to prepare anonymized request traces and confirm internal timeline and $ target.
[12:40] James: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[12:44] Evan: Thank you. We'll follow up tomorrow with the materials.
[12:48] Call ended.
